A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LieRE research despite the changed title and presentation. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification results on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k, and UCF101, together with scaling, efficiency, and patch-shuffling experiments.

after.justification: v3 reports original results on the retained benchmarks and adds synthetic spatial classification, resolution generalization, and appendix diagnostics.

M1.justification: v2's stem-shared LieRE configuration is replaced by separate learned bases for each attention head and layer by default in v3 Section 4 and Figure 2. The matrix-exponential encoding and key/query rotations remain intact; LieRE8 and LieRE64 emphasize configurations within the existing block-diagonal method family.

E1.justification: CIFAR-100, ImageNet-1k, and UCF101 remain. v3 adds a synthetic arrow-and-letter spatial reasoning task at multiple resolutions and ImageNet evaluation at resolutions unseen during training, substantially extending task and test-scenario coverage.

E2.justification: The three main external encoding baselines remain, but RoPE-Mixed is added to the compute-reduction plot (v2 Figure 4b versus v3 Figure 10). LieRE-Commute loses its separate main-benchmark rows, while its shared configuration remains represented in the sharing ablation. v3 also reports qualitative synthetic-task failures for ChatGPT 4o, Claude Sonnet 3.5, and Gemini Pro 1.5.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 changes the reported video input from 32 to 8 frames. New protocols include synthetic training on 800,000 examples with a 2-million-example absolute-encoding control, and ImageNet evaluation with optional 30-epoch fine-tuning at 256 × 256. Validation loss is newly reported. These establish reported setting changes without proving which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds resolution robustness tests, synthetic-task attention-map case studies, and raw/smoothed training and validation curves. Basis-capacity analysis expands from CIFAR-100 to UCF101, while parameter-sharing and patch-shuffling analyses receive revised evidence (Figure 8, Tables 3–4, and Appendix B.9–B.12).

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals, explicitly described as bootstrapped in Table 5, and display uncertainty on scaling plots. v3 extends this practice to additional results but reports no new run counts, seeds, significance-testing procedures, or uncertainty-estimation methods.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes RoPE-Mixed scores from 63.7 to 68.8 on CIFAR-100 and 65.9 to 68.8 on ImageNet. Numerous LieRE, scaling, shuffling, FLOP, and efficiency results also change; UCF101 scores are replaced under the reported shorter-clip setting. New results include synthetic accuracy, resolution curves, and validation losses; at 276 × 276, Table 2 reports 100% for LieRE64 versus 88.6% for RoPE-Mixed.

T1.justification: Equation (2) corrects its final expression from exp(U)^(-1) exp(V) to exp(V)^(-1) exp(U), fixing the incorrect inverse placement. The underlying Lie-group argument remains, and no new theorem or proof is added. The new attention background mainly explains existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces headline 2D/3D gains of up to 9.7%/25.5% over the listed baselines with approximately 2%/1.5% over state-of-the-art baselines. It adds a higher-resolution generalization claim, and the introduction claims that the synthetic spatial task requires relative encodings. Cross-modal applicability and efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 favors shared parameters and describes accuracy increasing with generator capacity; v3 favors learning across heads/layers and identifies an 8 × 8 block optimum. Its data-efficiency interpretation now credits both LieRE and RoPE-Mixed. Resolution-invariance and attention-to-Y interpretations are added, while the architectural and SE(3) limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds synthetic-data construction details, the 1e-5 cosine fine-tuning schedule, positional scaling instructions, and attention-map normalization. Most existing optimizer, hardware, and Python implementation information remains. v3 claims code release but removes v2's direct LieRE repository link; actual availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds Lee et al. (2022) to contextualize training baselines and Shah et al. (2024) for the synthetic task. It removes v2's claim to provide the first training-efficiency comparison of the recent methods. The main related-work taxonomy and cited positional-encoding literature remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Related work becomes a separate section, attention background is added, and separate Experiments/Results sections become task-organized experiments. Efficiency discussions move to the appendix, the conclusion precedes limitations, and the title and author list change.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns with substantial display reflow. Figure 2 is redrawn, earlier multipanel plots are separated and relocated, and efficiency/FLOP displays move to the appendix. New synthetic-task, resolution, learning-curve, attention-map, and validation-loss displays substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The synthetic spatial task and resolution tests (Table 2 and Figure 9) provide more direct evidence about positional reasoning and generalization than v2's classification and shuffling experiments. Equation (2) is corrected, and appendix diagnostics make the empirical behavior easier to assess. These gains are tempered by incomplete LLM evaluation details, removal of the direct code link, and unreconciled compute-saving claims of 3.9× in Appendix B.6 versus 3.5× in the conclusion.
